title: Accountability jeers that stick
lede: The wrong leaderboard now deals one shared three-line set from a 50-jeer deck. Everyone sees the same joke, reloads keep it put, and a meaningful leaderboard change earns fresh material.

stats.n: Exactly 50 unique, source-owned jeers generated with GPT-5.6 Luna Max
No duplicate line can appear within one spotlight set
ADMIN, STAFF, and STUDENT receive identical copy for identical board state
Reloads stay fixed; membership, order, or incident changes reshuffle

sections.heading: Same board, fresher voice
sections.note: Matched signed-in Admin session, 2026–27 filter, Volume ranking, 1440×1000 viewport, data, and layout. Only the spotlight copy source changes.

pairs.title: The top-three spotlight
pairs.sub: Fixed rank copy becomes a stable shared deal from the reviewed deck.
pairs.beforeCap: The same three rank-specific lines appear on every visit.
pairs.afterCap: Three distinct lines are selected from the shared 50-line deck and stay attached to this board state.

changes.h: Fixed copy became a shared deck
changes.was: Each podium rank had one hard-coded sentence, so repeat visits quickly felt familiar.
changes.now: The API returns three unique lines from a reviewed 50-line source deck alongside the leaderboard.

changes.was: Per-viewer or per-render randomness would let people see different jokes and would churn on refresh.
changes.now: A deterministic seeded shuffle uses the ordered leaderboard fingerprint, producing the same deal for every internal role and render environment.

changes.h: The joke waits for new material
changes.was: A background refresh or continuously increasing late-hours value could have changed copy without a real leaderboard event.
changes.now: The fingerprint ignores clock-only hour drift and changes for membership, ranking order, active state, late-event count, active-overdue count, or last incident.

changes.was: Generating copy on demand would add latency, cost, and unpredictable output to a simple report read.
changes.now: Luna Max generated the reviewed source deck once; serving and rotating it is local, bounded, and deterministic.

verification: Focused contracts: 64 Accountability, deck, route, service, RBAC, search, sidebar, and UI tests pass.
Static/build: TypeScript, focused ESLint, docs/codemap verification, whitespace check, and the 238-page build:app pass.
Shared API contract: ADMIN, STAFF, and STUDENT receive the same three unique jeers for identical leaderboard input; unchanged cloned input returns the same draw.
Authenticated browser: Volume reloads retained the exact same three lines. Time changed leaderboard order and produced a distinct three-line set; returning to Volume restored the original set.
Responsive render: 1440×1000 and 1024×900 show all three lines with zero horizontal overflow and no console warnings or errors.
notes: The selector guarantees no duplicate within a served set. Future distinct leaderboard states can eventually revisit a line because the product does not keep a durable history of every prior draw.
Clock-only total-late-hours movement is excluded from the seed, but a Time-sort order change still rotates the set because ordered rank is part of the fingerprint.
There is no runtime model call, browser storage, per-user seed, database write, or deployment in this slice.
